FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Miami, Florida
January 21, 1998

RESPONSE TO CABINET RESOLUTION OPPOSING MEDICAL USE OF MARIJUANA

Today the Governor's cabinet adopted a resolution opposing the medical use of marijuana and efforts by Florida citizens to place this issue on the ballot. This resolution was passed despite the fact that no medical testimony was presented.

"This type of political posturing sacrifices serious health needs of Floridians and deprives them of medical treatment that many physicians consider legitimate," said Toni Leeman, president of the Coalition Advocating Medical Marijuana.

Leading medical journals such as The Journal of the American Medical Association and The New England Journal of Medicine report many documented medical uses of marijuana including (1) relief of nausea due to cancer chemotherapy treatments, (2) nausea relief and appetite stimulation for AIDS patients suffering from wasting syndrome, and (3) the reduction of intraocular pressure for people with glaucoma. Marijuana has also been documented to relieve muscle spasticity problems for people with multiple sclerosis and paraplegics.

Floridians for Medical Rights has undertaken a petition initiative to place this issue on the ballot because Florida government leaders have failed to address the medical use of marijuana. A recent Florida Voter poll reported that 63% of voters would approve such a measure if it were to appear on the ballot. "It is disappointing that our elected officials don't represent the will of the people on this issue," Leeman added.

"Today we saw public policy developed in a vacuum of ignorance," said Howard Simon, Executive Director of the American Civil Liberties Union of Florida. "This is nothing more than a ploy to try to prevent this issue from appearing on the ballot. We think voters have the intelligence to see through the propaganda and approve needed medical treatment -- as they did in Arizona and California."

A petition drive is now underway to place a proposed constitutional amendment before the voters. Copies of the petition are available by contacting Floridians for Medical Rights at (954) 537-3150 or writing to P.O. Box 290054, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33329-0054. E-mail:calmmfl@aol.com
